q: In which year did India initiate family planning programmes, which were later broadened into the RCH programmes?
India was among the first countries in the world to launch national action plans for a reproductively healthy society, beginning with family planning programmes in…
The statutory ban on amniocentesis in India applies specifically to its use for:
Detecting genetic disorders of the foetus
Determining the sex of the foetus
Amniocentesis remains legal and valuable for detecting genetic disorders and chromosomal abnormalities. Only its misuse for foetal sex determination — which led to…
‘Saheli’, the non-steroidal once-a-week oral contraceptive for females, was developed by:
Saheli was developed by scientists at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow. It is a non-steroidal preparation taken once a week, with very few side…
The world population rose from about 2 billion in 1900 to approximately how much by the year 2000?
The world population was around 2 billion (2000 million) in 1900 and rose dramatically to about 6 billion by 2000 — roughly a threefold increase in a single century.
The statutory minimum marriageable age in India for females and males respectively is:
As a step to control population growth, the marriageable age has been raised by statute to 18 years for females and 21 years for males.
In the periodic abstinence (rhythm) method, coitus is avoided during which days of the menstrual cycle?
Days 10 to 17 form the fertile period of a normal cycle, when ovulation is expected and the chances of fertilisation are highest, so coitus is avoided during this window.
The lactational amenorrhea method is effective only up to a maximum of:
During intense lactation the mother does not menstruate or ovulate, so conception chances are almost nil — but this protection lasts only up to a maximum of 6 months…
The method in which the male partner withdraws the penis from the vagina just before ejaculation is called:
Coitus interruptus, also called the withdrawal method, is a natural contraceptive method in which semen is prevented from being deposited in the female reproductive…
Lippes loop is an example of which type of intra uterine device?
The Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD. It acts by causing a sterile inflammatory response that produces minor tissue injury sufficient to be spermicidal.
Oral contraceptive pills are taken daily for 21 days beginning:
Within the first 5 days of the menstrual cycle
On any convenient day of the cycle
The pill is started within the first 5 days of the menstrual cycle and taken daily for 21 days, followed by a gap of 7 days during which menstruation occurs; the same…
Emergency contraceptives are effective in avoiding pregnancy if used within:
Administration of progesterone, a progesterone–oestrogen combination, or insertion of an IUD within 72 hours of coitus is very effective as emergency contraception,…
In vasectomy, sterilisation is achieved by removing or tying off a part of which structure?
Vasectomy blocks sperm transport by removing/tying a small part of the vas deferens through a scrotal incision.
In which year did India legalise Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP)?
India legalised MTP in 1971, with strict conditions to prevent misuse such as female foeticide.
Tubectomy involves removing/tying a part of the fallopian tube, blocking ova transport.
Which of these STDs is NOT completely curable even with treatment?
Except hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV, all other STDs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
Besides unsafe sexual contact, hepatitis-B and HIV can also spread through:
Hepatitis-B and HIV can additionally spread via infected needles/syringes, blood transfusion, or from mother to foetus.
A late, untreated complication of an STD in which the blastocyst implants outside the uterus is called:
Ectopic pregnancy — implantation of the blastocyst outside the uterus — is a late complication of untreated STDs.
The age group reporting the highest incidence of STDs is:
Highest incidence of STDs is reported in the 15–24 years age group.
A sperm count below 20 million/ml is termed:
Oligospermia is a deficiency in sperm count, below 20 million/ml (normal is 50–150 million/ml).
Complete absence of sperm in the ejaculate is called:
Azoospermia refers to complete absence of sperm in the ejaculate.
Absence of one or both testes from the scrotum
Cryptorchidism (Greek: kryptos = hidden, orchis = testis) is the absence of one or both testes from the scrotum.
By clinical definition, a couple is generally considered infertile if they fail to conceive despite regular unprotected intercourse for:
Infertility is commonly defined as inability to conceive after about 2 years of regular unprotected intercourse.
IVF is popularly known as the:
IVF (In Vitro Fertilisation), where fertilisation occurs outside the body followed by embryo transfer, is popularly called the 'test tube baby' method.
In ZIFT, the zygote transferred into the fallopian tube is at which stage?
In ZIFT, the zygote is transferred into the fallopian tube up to the 8-blastomere stage; beyond that (IUT) it goes to the uterus.
Promoting equal opportunity for the male and female child and discouraging sex-based discrimination is listed as an aim of:
One of the major aims of the RCH programme is promoting equal opportunity for the male and female child and discouraging sex-based discrimination.
India's population at the time of independence (1947) was approximately:
India's population was about 350 million at independence (1947); it crossed 1 billion by May 2000.
“HUM DO HAMARE DO” is a slogan used in India to promote:
Free distribution of oral contraceptive pills
A one- or two-child family norm
The slogan “HUM DO HAMARE DO” (we two, our two) is used as part of education and motivation campaigns promoting a one- or two-child family norm.
Barrier methods, IUDs, oral pills and surgical sterilisation are all examples of:
Artificial methods physically or chemically prevent the union of ovum and sperm; they include barriers, IUDs, oral pills, injectables/implants and surgical sterilisation.
Condoms and diaphragms are both classified as:
Condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are all barrier methods that physically prevent the ovum and sperm from meeting.
A major reason for the increased use of condoms in recent years, besides preventing pregnancy, is that they:
Increase the sexual drive of the user
Are the only method approved for males
Condoms are disposable, self-inserted, give privacy, and importantly protect against STDs and AIDS — which is why their use has increased greatly.
Depo Provera is an example of a contraceptive given as a(n):
Depo Provera is a progesterone injectable contraceptive; its mode of action is similar to the pills but its effective period is much longer.
Approximately what fraction of the total number of conceived pregnancies worldwide end in an MTP every year?
Around 45–50 million MTPs are performed worldwide every year, which is about one-fifth of the total number of conceived pregnancies.
MTPs conducted illegally by unqualified quacks are considered an unhealthy trend mainly because they:
Are more expensive than legal MTPs
Take much longer to perform than legal MTPs
Are unsafe and could even be fatal to the mother
Are always performed after the second trimester
MTPs conducted illegally by unqualified quacks are unsafe and could even be fatal to the mother — a major unhealthy trend associated with MTP.
In tubectomy, a small part of which structure is removed or tied off?
In tubectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied off, blocking the transport of ova and preventing fertilisation.
Asthenozoospermia, one of the male causes of infertility, refers to:
Complete absence of sperms in the ejaculate
Absence of one or both testes from the scrotum
Asthenozoospermia is poor motility of sperms, distinct from oligospermia (low count), azoospermia (no sperm at all) and cryptorchidism (undescended testes).
Non-canalisation of the vagina and improper development of the uterus are causes of infertility specific to:
Non-canalisation of the vagina, improper uterine development and uterine tumours are causes of infertility in women.
In artificial insemination (AI), if using the husband's own semen is not possible, semen may instead be collected from:
In AI, semen collected from the husband or, alternatively, from a donor is artificially introduced into the female's vagina or uterus.
In artificial insemination (AI), semen from the husband or a donor is introduced into the female's:
In AI, semen collected from the husband or a donor is artificially introduced either into the vagina or into the uterus of the female.
Which contraceptive device works primarily by releasing ions that suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms?
Multiload 375 (like CuT and Cu7) is a copper-releasing IUD; the released Cu ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity. Lippes loop is non-medicated…
India’s population, which was about 350 million at the time of independence, crossed 1 billion by:
India’s population was roughly 350 million in 1947 and crossed the 1 billion mark by May 2000, making every sixth person in the world an Indian.
Tubectomy, a surgical contraceptive method in females, involves:
Removal/tying of a part of the fallopian tube
Tubectomy blocks ova transport by removing or tying off a part of the fallopian tube.
The statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination was implemented mainly to prevent:
Amniocentesis was banned for sex determination to prevent its misuse in aborting female foetuses (female foeticide).
Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) is best described as a:
Late complication of an untreated STD
PID is a late/untreated complication of STDs that can lead to infertility.
STDs show the highest reported incidence in which age group?
The 15–24 years age group reports the highest incidence of STDs.
Which of these is a male cause of infertility?
Cryptorchidism (absence of testes from the scrotum) is a male cause of infertility.
Normal human sperm count is generally considered to be in the range of:
Normal sperm count is 50–150 million/ml; a count below 20 million/ml is termed oligospermia.
Infertility is clinically defined as failure to conceive despite regular unprotected intercourse for about:
Infertility is commonly defined as failure to conceive after about 2 years of regular unprotected intercourse.
In IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer), the embryo transferred to the uterus is at a stage of:
In IUT, embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred directly into the uterus.
Which ART technique involves transferring a donor ovum into another female's fallopian tube for fertilisation to occur within her body?
In GIFT, a donor ovum is transferred into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce her own ova but can support fertilisation/development.
A fall in the number of illegal abortions performed and a reduction in the incidence of infertility in a population are both regarded as:
Side effects of oral contraceptive pills
Reduced number of illegal abortions and reduced infertility are both listed among the indicators of improved reproductive health of a society.
Population explosion directly leads to scarcity of basic requirements such as food, shelter and clothing, and also increases:
Availability of natural resources per person
The number of fertility clinics automatically
Population explosion causes scarcity of basic requirements and increases unemployment, poverty and pressure on natural resources.
According to the chapter, a contraceptive method should ideally be chosen only after:
Reading an advertisement in a newspaper
Checking its price at a local pharmacy
The chapter emphasises that the choice of a contraceptive method should always be made under consultation with a qualified medical professional.
‘Nirodh’ is a popular Indian brand name for which contraceptive device?
‘Nirodh’ is a popular brand of the male condom in India.
Amenorrhea, the basis of the term ‘lactational amenorrhea method’, refers to:
Amenorrhea means absence of menstruation; during intense lactation after parturition, the mother does not menstruate and does not ovulate.
A condom used by a female partner, unlike the male condom which covers the penis, is designed to cover:
Condoms are used to cover the penis in the male, or to cover the vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus.
LNG-20, a hormone-releasing IUD that releases levonorgestrel at 20 µg/day, is also sold under the trade name:
LNG-20 (Levonorgestrel 20 µg/day) is a hormone-releasing IUD also sold under the trade name Minera.
Injuries or disease of the ovaries, and non-ovulatory menstrual cycles, are listed in this chapter as causes of infertility specific to:
Endocrine disorders, injuries or disease of the ovaries, and non-ovulatory menstrual cycles are listed among the causes of infertility in women.
The acronym GIFT, an ART technique described in this chapter, stands for:
GIFT stands for Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer, in which a donor ovum is transferred into the fallopian tube of a recipient female.
The acronym ZIFT, an ART technique described in this chapter, stands for:
ZIFT stands for Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer, in which a laboratory-formed zygote (up to the 8-blastomere stage) is transferred into the fallopian tube.
The term ‘in vitro’ in In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) literally indicates that fertilisation of the ovum by the sperm takes place:
Inside the fallopian tube of the female
Outside the body, under laboratory conditions
Inside the testes of the male
In Vitro Fertilisation means fertilisation occurring outside the body, in a laboratory, followed by transfer of the embryo into the reproductive tract.
